Source: none. This notebook audits the outcome stage: the within-municipality
normalized deforestation increment on its two pre-treatment reference windows
and the exposure offset for the Poisson specifications, with the diagnostics
the legacy script printed to the console. Since phase 2R the pipeline stores
the main window only (D-2026-10-30-e); the short-window outcome is rebuilt
here with the shared `norm_within()`, and the sample panel is read through
the crosswalk so that both objects carry the final names (D-2026-10-30-a).
Pipeline script: `_scripts/06-normalized-outcome.R`.
Final output: `_data/final/panel_amz_2000_2020_final.rds`.
Equivalence with the recovered panel is not checked here (the notebook never
reads `_data/reference/`); the `compare_outputs` report lives in the phase 1
script 06 commit message and in the decision entries it cites.

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
})
options(width = 110)
```

```{r read}
source("_scripts/utils/crosswalk.R")
source("_scripts/utils/derived_variables.R")
xwalk <- read_crosswalk()
panel_in <- read_rds("_data/interim/panel_amz_2000_2020_sample.rds") %>%
  rename_through_crosswalk(xwalk)
REF_SHORT <- 2000:2003
REF_MAIN  <- 2000:2007
SD_FLOOR  <- 1e-9
panel <- read_rds("_data/final/panel_amz_2000_2020_final.rds") %>%
  norm_within("env_defor_area_km2", REF_SHORT, "env_defor_area_z_bl0003",
              SD_FLOOR)
SAMPLES <- c("all", "smp_avail_dum", "smp_atrisk_broad_dum", "smp_atrisk_narrow_dum")
in_sample <- function(d, s) if (s == "all") d else filter(d, .data[[s]])
```

## Q1. Is the sample panel complete, and are the two input series fit for the construction?

The construction needs a gapless, non-negative deforestation series and a
strictly positive forest area (the offset is a log).

```{r q1}
tibble(
  municipalities = n_distinct(panel_in$geocode),
  rows = nrow(panel_in),
  columns = ncol(panel_in),
  years = paste(range(panel_in$year), collapse = "-"),
  defor_na = sum(is.na(panel_in$env_defor_area_km2)),
  defor_min = min(panel_in$env_defor_area_km2),
  defor_zero_cells = sum(panel_in$env_defor_area_km2 == 0),
  forest_na = sum(is.na(panel_in$env_forest_area_km2)),
  forest_min = round(min(panel_in$env_forest_area_km2), 1)
)
panel_in %>%
  filter(env_defor_area_km2 == 0) %>%
  count(municipality, uf, name = "zero_years") %>%
  arrange(desc(zero_years)) %>%
  head(10)
```

**Finding.** 502 municipalities over 2000-2020, 82 columns; neither series
has a gap, clearing is never negative and the smallest forest area is about
35 km², so the log offset is defined everywhere a lag exists. Zero clearing
occurs in 38 municipality-years in six municipalities of the Marajó
archipelago, Amapá and the upper Rio Negro; Santa Cruz do Arari records zero
in every year.

**Decision.** D-2026-10-12-f, D-2026-10-12-g.

**Assertion.** `06-normalized-outcome.R`, raw-state block (dimensions,
types, no NA, non-negative clearing, positive forest area).

## Q2. Which municipalities have a degenerate or near-degenerate reference, and are any of them at risk?

A municipality whose clearing does not vary over the reference window has a
zero reference sd and cannot be normalized; the script sets its outcome to
NA. Municipalities with a small but non-zero sd are normalized, and a small
denominator inflates their values.

```{r q2}
ref_sd <- panel_in %>%
  group_by(geocode, municipality, uf,
           smp_avail_dum, smp_atrisk_broad_dum, smp_atrisk_narrow_dum) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_short = mean(env_defor_area_km2[year %in% REF_SHORT]),
    sd_short   = sd(env_defor_area_km2[year %in% REF_SHORT]),
    mean_main  = mean(env_defor_area_km2[year %in% REF_MAIN]),
    sd_main    = sd(env_defor_area_km2[year %in% REF_MAIN]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ref_sd %>%
  filter(sd_short <= SD_FLOOR | sd_main <= SD_FLOOR) %>%
  select(municipality, uf, smp_avail_dum, smp_atrisk_broad_dum,
         mean_short, sd_short, mean_main, sd_main)
ref_sd %>%
  filter(sd_main < 0.1) %>%
  arrange(sd_main) %>%
  select(municipality, uf, smp_avail_dum, smp_atrisk_broad_dum,
         mean_main, sd_main)
tibble(
  degenerate_short = sum(ref_sd$sd_short <= SD_FLOOR),
  degenerate_main = sum(ref_sd$sd_main <= SD_FLOOR),
  sd_main_below_0_1 = sum(ref_sd$sd_main < 0.1),
  of_which_at_risk_broad = sum(ref_sd$sd_main < 0.1 & ref_sd$smp_atrisk_broad_dum),
  na_cells_short = sum(is.na(panel$env_defor_area_z_bl0003)),
  na_cells_main = sum(is.na(panel$env_defor_area_z_bl0007))
)
```

**Finding.** Two municipalities are degenerate on the short window, Afuá
(PA) and Santa Cruz do Arari (PA), and one on the main window, Santa Cruz do
Arari, which records no clearing at all over 2000-2007. Their outcome is NA
over all 21 years (42 and 21 cells). Fourteen municipalities have a main
window sd below 0.1 km², all in the Marajó archipelago, Amapá and the upper
Amazonas; none of them, and neither degenerate municipality, is in the broad
at-risk sample, so the rule costs no estimation observation.

**Decision.** D-2026-10-12-f.

**Assertion.** `06-normalized-outcome.R`, output block (2 and 1 degenerate
municipalities, 21 NA cells each, none at risk).

## Q3. How is the normalized outcome distributed in the full panel and inside the estimation samples?

The parked prose claims heavy tails in the full panel from the
near-degenerate municipalities, and a well-behaved outcome within the
at-risk sample, with the bulk between about minus three and plus six on the
main reference.

```{r q3}
q_tbl <- function(x) {
  tibble(min = min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         p01 = quantile(x, .01, na.rm = TRUE),
         p05 = quantile(x, .05, na.rm = TRUE),
         med = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         p95 = quantile(x, .95, na.rm = TRUE),
         p99 = quantile(x, .99, na.rm = TRUE),
         max = max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         n_na = sum(is.na(x)))
}
map_dfr(SAMPLES, function(s) {
  d <- in_sample(panel, s)
  bind_rows(
    q_tbl(d$env_defor_area_z_bl0003) %>% mutate(outcome = "ref0003"),
    q_tbl(d$env_defor_area_z_bl0007) %>% mutate(outcome = "ref0007")
  ) %>% mutate(sample = s, n = nrow(d))
}) %>%
  select(sample, outcome, n, everything()) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2)))
panel %>%
  filter(smp_atrisk_narrow_dum) %>%
  arrange(desc(env_defor_area_z_bl0007)) %>%
  select(municipality, uf, year, env_defor_area_km2,
         env_defor_area_z_bl0007) %>%
  head(8)
panel %>%
  arrange(desc(env_defor_area_z_bl0007)) %>%
  select(municipality, uf, year, smp_atrisk_broad_dum,
         env_defor_area_km2, env_defor_area_z_bl0007) %>%
  head(8)
```

**Finding.** In the full panel the main-reference outcome reaches 250
(Chaves, PA, 2011, on 1.7 km² cleared) and 176 (São Gabriel da Cachoeira,
AM, 2020): the near-degenerate municipalities of Q2, all outside the
at-risk samples. Inside the narrow sample the central 98 percent of the
main-reference outcome lies between about minus three and plus four and a
half, so the parked claim holds with room; the maximum is 42 (Feijó, AC,
2019), and the top of the distribution is the 2019-2020 clearing surge in
Acre and southern Amazonas (Feijó, Humaitá, Assis Brasil, Manoel Urbano).
The short-reference outcome has the wider tails on both sides, as its
four-year sd is smaller.

**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-h (estimation on the at-risk sample); any
winsorising is a modelling decision, not a pipeline one.

**Assertion.** None beyond finiteness; the tails are a property of the
estimation sample, documented here.

## Q4. How much do the two reference windows disagree on each municipality's scale, and does the centring matter?

The two windows differ in the sd that sets each municipality's scale. Under
municipality fixed effects only that sd enters the estimate, since the
subtracted mean is absorbed; the second table checks that identity
numerically.

```{r q4}
ratio <- ref_sd %>%
  filter(sd_short > SD_FLOOR, sd_main > SD_FLOOR) %>%
  mutate(sd_ratio = sd_main / sd_short)
map_dfr(SAMPLES, function(s) {
  d <- in_sample(ratio, s)
  tibble(sample = s, n = nrow(d),
         p05 = quantile(d$sd_ratio, .05), p25 = quantile(d$sd_ratio, .25),
         med = median(d$sd_ratio), p75 = quantile(d$sd_ratio, .75),
         p95 = quantile(d$sd_ratio, .95),
         cor_outcomes = cor(in_sample(panel, s)$env_defor_area_z_bl0003,
                            in_sample(panel, s)$env_defor_area_z_bl0007,
                            use = "complete.obs"))
}) %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
demeaned <- panel %>%
  filter(!is.na(env_defor_area_z_bl0007)) %>%
  left_join(select(ref_sd, geocode, sd_main), by = "geocode") %>%
  group_by(geocode) %>%
  mutate(y_ref = env_defor_area_z_bl0007 - mean(env_defor_area_z_bl0007),
         y_alt = env_defor_area_km2 / sd_main -
           mean(env_defor_area_km2 / sd_main)) %>%
  ungroup()
tibble(max_abs_gap = max(abs(demeaned$y_ref - demeaned$y_alt)))
```

**Finding.** The main-window sd is larger than the short-window sd for
most municipalities (median ratio 1.1, upper quartile 1.5, top five
percent above 2.8), as 2004-2007 adds the mid-2000s peak to the reference.
The two outcomes correlate at about 0.8 within the at-risk samples and only
0.4 in the full panel, where the near-degenerate municipalities dominate.
The within-municipality demeaned outcome is numerically identical whether
the increment is centred on the reference mean or not centred at all, which
is the property the parked prose states: the window fixes the scale, not
the centre.

**Decision.** D-2026-10-12-f (main 2000-2007, short 2000-2003 as the
robustness alternative; flagged for the storage audit, task 2.2, because
the window is a robustness parameter).

**Assertion.** `06-normalized-outcome.R`, constants block (the column
names are generated from the window constants and tied by assertion).

## Q5. Is the exposure offset defined where the Poisson specification needs it?

```{r q5}
panel %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(na_offset = sum(is.na(env_forest_exposure_log)),
            min_offset = round(min(env_forest_exposure_log), 2),
            max_offset = round(max(env_forest_exposure_log), 2),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(year <= 2002 | year == max(year))
panel %>%
  filter(year > min(year)) %>%
  group_by(geocode) %>%
  summarise(lag_ok = all(abs(exp(env_forest_exposure_log) -
                               lag(env_forest_area_km2, default = NA)) < 1e-6,
                         na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  count(lag_ok)
```

**Finding.** The offset is missing in 2000 only (502 cells) and finite
everywhere else, between about 3.6 and 12 (35 km² to 160,000 km² of
standing forest); exponentiating it returns the previous year's forest area
exactly. The Poisson specifications therefore lose one year per
municipality and no municipality.

**Decision.** D-2026-10-12-g.

**Assertion.** `06-normalized-outcome.R`, output block (NA in the first
year only, finite elsewhere).
